paper.title: Library Drift: Diagnosing and Fixing a Silent Failure Mode in Self-Evolving LLM Skill Libraries
paper.central_claim: Unbounded skill accumulation without lifecycle management causes library drift; trace-level diagnostics isolate it and retirement, a bounded bank and meta-skill authoring prior prevent drift, improve held-out performance and provide a non-divergence guarantee.

evidence.quote:
A meta-skill document constrains the Synthesizer to produce
stylistically consistent skills. This addresses the “silent
injection harm” stage at its source: by enforcing structural
homogeneity, fewer harmful or redundant skills are born in the
first place, reducing the load on downstream retirement. Ablation
A3 (no meta-skill) shows that removing it costs 43% of the
Default’s gain; it is the single most valuable component.

Surprisingly, explicit deduplication mechanisms (pattern
canonicalisation, A5; cover-guard, A6) are
not
necessary
given the meta-skill: A5 and A6 slightly
exceed
the
Default. The meta-skill subsumes explicit dedup at this scale, a
design insight relevant to any system with LLM-authored artifacts.
evidence.support_explanation: Meta-skill is an authoring prior; explicit deduplication can be unnecessary, a useful negative result.

gap.author_gap: Growing LLM-authored libraries may stagnate or regress; existing systems allegedly lack outcome-driven retirement plus bounded cap.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete unanswered questions are which retained entries help and whether conservative retirement prevents harm. The paper shows injection matters and aggressive retirement can hurt, but does not isolate the asserted unbounded-accumulation causal chain. Prior novelty claims remain author positioning.

rs_pattern.reason: Revised. The paper names the load-bearing implicit assumption of Voyager-style libraries ('compounding': each deposited skill helps) and pivots the budgeted retention rule. Append-only becomes outcome-driven retirement with an evidence floor and a hard cap, plus a re-derived certificate (Prop. 1). That is C11's object (which elements stay in a budgeted selection) and its documented failure shape: a guarantee that does not hold up (contribution ≠ treatment effect; vacuous floor E[p0]−0.35) and no 'revert the pivot' arm (no retirement-off / uncapped control). son55 picked the right parent but left sub=null; sol's controlled_diagnostic_design/C02 is kept as supporting for the trace-diagnostics and null-injection contribution. C02 fit is partial because no controlled instance set is built. sol's supporting adapt_via_conditioning is not kept: conditioning a frozen solver on stored skills is the shared substrate, not this paper's move.

G.reason: Opus = sol. Lifecycle governance is a real, sourced concern (survey, SkillsBench), and neighbours are named with specific differences. But the gap premise (unbounded accumulation causes drift) is not demonstrated in the paper's own setting: A1 is injection-off and A4 is over-governance. The cited symptom (LLM-authored skills +0.0pp) is an authoring finding, and the paper's own A3 makes authoring the largest component (opus:O06/O07). The problem position is therefore partly contradicted by its own evidence.

M.reason: Both seats 2, confirmed. The feedback → synthesis → retirement/cap mechanism is concrete. But Eq. 2 is not a treatment effect relative to p0, harder-task skills are retired by construction, and Prop. 1's proof equates the two.

X.reason: Opus = sol. Router, synthesis trigger, retirement floor, cap and hyperparameters are given, and code is linked. Key retention conditions are unclear or contradictory. Rollback appears only in the hyperparameter table, with no trigger data or semantics (son55:E030). Whether the curator's evidence log excludes eval capsules is unstated (sol:E016). Table 1's A1 row contradicts the synthesis/retirement rules (opus:O01–O03).

E.measurement.reason: Opus = sol. MBPP+ pass@1 with executable tests is credible, and the single-call solver isolates the library. But the diagnostic metrics the paper offers as a contribution are unvalidated: Eq. 2 is labelled 'contribution' but measures conditional success, and the early-warning claim rests on one case (A4). The A1 table row is internally inconsistent (opus:O01). This is the run's cap of 2 for table–mechanism contradictions.

E.causality.reason: Both seats 2, confirmed. A1 (same pipeline, injection off) is a strong store-off control, and A2/A3 attribute the gate and the meta-skill. There is no retirement-off or uncapped arm, so 'retirement and cap are load-bearing' is untested; A7 doubles the cap and keeps the mean. A4 changes two knobs, and there is no external ungoverned baseline.

E.holdout.reason: Opus = sol. The 60/40 split is stated and skill content comes from train failures, but the method's selection step may read the evaluation set. The router injects on the 40 eval tasks every round (Appendix A Eval phase), Eq. 2 is computed from 'capsules where s was injected' with no train-only restriction, and the undocumented rollback likely monitors the same score. The same 40 tasks are reused across 100 rounds, all 9 conditions and empirically chosen thresholds. Tasks are filtered by the same model, contamination is not checked, and there is one benchmark. The paper's 'held-out' label is thus not protected.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 2, confirmed (A2 tier 2): 3 seeds with std and a per-seed table, and negative results. No CI or test, n=40 eval tasks.

E.cost.reason: Opus = sol. Calls and wall time are disclosed (Default vs A1, A8 10.1 h). But the 14.5k tally omits per-task LLM router-gate calls (opus:O04/O05), there is no token/dollar accounting, and no budget-matched alternative.
